description: Each question was asked once, in a fresh ADK session, through the running API (POST /run, app 'app'). System answers and retrieved context come from the ADK events; costs come from the model_call_usage ledger. Expected answers were read from the live ameriabank.am pages and linked PDFs on the same day.

system_under_test.entry_point: ADK POST /run on the api container (http://localhost:8081), one new session per question

ground_truth.method: All 13 seed pages and 27 linked PDFs downloaded (HTTP 200). Product tabs are loaded by JavaScript from https://ameriabank.am/API/WebsitesCreative/MyContentManager/API/Init?portalId=0&tabId=<tabId>&moduleId=<id>; that JSON was fetched and rendered. PDF text via PyMuPDF with page markers. Every quote was re-checked against the saved text.
caveats: The 12.9% shown on six mortgage heroes is a campaign rate (1 Jul - 30 Dec 2026, active); tariff tables show higher standard rates.
Hero banners conflict with tariff tables on Commercial (36-360 vs 60/61-360 months; APR), Renovation (APR), Construction (360 vs 61-240) and Express (60-360 vs 61-360).
Diaspora: no validity dates and no linked PDF; its USD/EUR rates match no other current mortgage tariff.
Online Consumer Finance: 17% appears only in the hero; the web terms table has empty interest-rate rows; the linked leaflet is generic.
Consumer loan: hidden SEO metadata still says AMD 10 million and 13.79-23.72%, against the visible AMD 20 million.

key_findings: No fabricated values in any of the 15 answers: every stated number traces to an accepted fact and its source (groundedness 1.0).
7 of 15 questions were answered correctly (Q4, Q7, Q8, Q12, Q13, Q14 and a correct abstention on Q9); all single-offering answers on published offerings were right.

Data coverage, not retrieval, dominates the failures: after all runs only 5 of 13 offerings had accepted data; 8 were held by 22 pending human reviews (none applied in this session), so Q5, Q10, Q11 and Q15 abstained.

Family rankings silently ignore offerings without accepted data (not_ranked lists none of them), so Q2 reported AMD 100M as the largest mortgage amount (truth: AMD 150M, six offerings) and Q3 named 2 of 8 offerings at 360 months.
Q1: Online Consumer Finance's 17% fact has no currency, so the AMD-restricted rank excluded it.
Q6: the interpreter read 'terms' as loan term only, so amount, rate, collateral and repayment were omitted.

Review queue quality: 12 of 22 reviews are validator false positives or formatting defects on correct values (income-verification check, JSON-string answers, stitched quotes); 8 come from one Commercial extraction call that failed the schema on two models; 2 are fields the source genuinely omits, which the review policy cannot accept as 'not stated'.

Every answer opens with the catalog intro and pending-review notice (the instruction treats each fresh session as a first turn), which buries the answer; Q6, Q8 and Q14 put the answer first and the intro after it.
